files.note: Which gaia-dr3 tile row each designated HIP number names: 2,649 rows in HIP order (catalog, catalogId, layer, pix, index, hip, link), evidenceKind 'catalog-derived', linked by HIP number only: 219 Hipparcos rows by their own HIP, 2,430 Gaia rows as the best neighbour of that HIP. No designation is in this file; the designations are ../designations/designations.json, under its own record and licence, joined by HIP number when read. The guard read HYG v4.1 (hygdata_v41.csv, sha256 d9f69fd86bbf90a4e4d52b4c5c53eacfa6dfc0bfdef85bfd94f095e0bebe4ebd) to decide which links are kept: which HIP numbers carry a designation, and each one's V, which is not written here. A Gaia row is kept only if its V, from its G and BP-RP by Riello et al. 2021 (A&A 649, A3, Table C.2, for -0.5 < BP-RP < 5.0), is at most 2.5 log10 2 mag fainter than HYG's V, so it holds at least half the star's light [proposed: a bound derived from half the light, not tuned; it drops a row rather than risk a wrong star]. Of 3,303 designated HIP numbers, set aside: 642 with no best neighbour, 0 whose neighbour is not a tile row, 8 fainter than half the light, 4 without a colour in range.
